title: Vaudeville rehearsals, costumes and the Chicago Theatre orchestra
summary: How acts were rehearsed quickly by sight reading, wearing costumes on stage in Chicago, and playing with a large European-born orchestra.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: That's good. Good numbers. Well, suppose a new act would come in. How would you play that? Would you have to rehearse with... Oh, yeah.
All these shows you rehearse. You're talking about...
Yeah, well, they have a two-hour rehearsal and you got about six or seven acts and everybody just tells you what they want, how the music... You run over maybe once and that's it.

But, uh, you have to be a sight reader, you know what I mean? Oh, yeah. Yeah. And at that time, uh, you know, you used to get some crazy music, like, uh, big overtures and all that stuff. You play, you see?
Did you ever have to get up on the stage or put on a costume or anything you said?

No, no. Well, you're not in the Palace. Yeah. Where would you put on a costume? When I went to Chicago, when I played in Chicago, we used to wear costumes, all kinds of costumes. Chinese outfits, Mexican outfits.
For different acts then? Yeah, I see. No, it just...
The show that would come in, you know, they put costumes.
Depends on what kind of show it was. Would you be in the pit in the costume or on the stage?
That'd make you get up on the stage?

Yeah. Oh, in the pit you rest just like you rest every day. But that was a good experience. I'll tell you, the best experience I ever had in music, when I played Chicago Theatre, was two trombones, three trumpets, and all about 25 fiddle players, and all that stuff. And it was beautiful to play that music. And when you get on the stage, you got something, it's like the contrast, you know? Something different, see? You're playing two types of music. Yeah, see? And I'll tell you, Dick, when I played at the Chicago Theatre, they had some fine musicians from Europe there. I think over half of the band, orchestra, let's say orchestra, was from Europe, from all over, Russia, Finland.
